subject.title: Per-agent tools.selfDeny — allow tool inheritance to subagents while denying direct use

question: Should OpenClaw add a parent-only/delegate-only tool policy surface, rely on per-spawn `toolsAllow`, or keep the current monotonic restriction invariant?
rationale: This is a public config and security-boundary decision: the code can implement several shapes, but only maintainers can choose whether a requester may withhold tools from itself while still delegating them to child sessions.

options.title: Design a unified delegate-only policy
options.body: Add one canonical parent-hidden/delegate-visible contract, align it with inherited allow/deny storage, and document how it composes with `tools.subagents.tools` and per-spawn restrictions.

options.title: Use per-spawn restrictions only
options.body: Make the `sessions_spawn.toolsAllow` direction the canonical path and leave this issue open only if it still cannot express the separation-of-duties case after that lands.

options.title: Keep monotonic restriction
options.body: Reject delegate-only escalation and document that operators must use separate configured agent identities or stricter child narrowing instead.

recommendation.title: Design a unified delegate-only policy
recommendation.body: Add one canonical parent-hidden/delegate-visible contract, align it with inherited allow/deny storage, and document how it composes with `tools.subagents.tools` and per-spawn restrictions.
